key_insight: Irradiation-induced vacancy loops in tungsten evolve during dislocation interactions in geometry-dependent ways, ranging from annihilation or transport to strong sessile defect formation, which changes obstacle strength.
engineering_relevance: These atomistic interaction rules can be converted into constitutive parameters for mesoscale models, improving predictions of irradiation hardening in fusion-relevant tungsten components.
method: Molecular dynamics simulations of edge dislocations interacting with vacancy loops in tungsten
Systematic variation of loop size, crystallographic orientation, and dislocation-loop intersection geometry
Translation of atomistic obstacle strengths into constitutive hardening parameters
evidence_signal: The abstract reports systematic simulation results across multiple interaction geometries and uses them to derive obstacle-strength trends and a framework for constitutive parameterization.
watch_item: The constitutive mapping is demonstrated from atomistic data, but broader model transfer will still need validation across wider defect populations, temperatures, and loading conditions.
paper_title: Evolution of the Irradiation Induced Defect Landscape through Dislocation Vacancy Loop Interactions in Tungsten
